target.title: fix: shell cron reminders still show unscheduled note
target.body:
Closes #52972

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who scheduled a one-time reminder through a successful shell command such as `openclaw cron add --at ...` could still receive the contradictory "I did not schedule a reminder" note in the same reply.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reminder guard already trusts structured cron-tool successes, but shell-driven cron adds pass through the exec/bash tool path. This change records successful shell `openclaw cron add --at` commands at the tool-result producer boundary using parsed command arguments and the exec completion status, without matching prose output or broad cron commands.

## User Impact

Users can schedule reminders through shell-based cron commands without seeing a false failure note after the cron job was created. Failed commands, unrelated cron commands, and non-reminder cron adds remain uncounted.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: successful `exec`/`bash` shell `openclaw cron add --at` commands increment `successfulCronAdds`, while failed shell commands, `cron list`, and cron adds without `--at` do not.
- Current head: `b60b1bb4db041409d20a2d4066888ea741608f04`.
- Commands:
  - `git diff --check` - passed.
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts` - passed, 86 tests.
- Observed result: focused regression coverage passed on this branch head.
- Not tested / proof gaps: no live Telegram reminder turn was run; the proof exercises the producer state that the reply guard consumes.
